body:
WHERE IT GOES, AND ONE TRAP (code read 6 Nov 2026, main e394d03; B-32 has the finding).

TODAY. App: `EncoreApi._options` (app/lib/data/encore/encore_api.dart:50-51) sets one header, `X-Encore-Device`, and nothing names a request; the ring buffer and Diagnostics exist (core/logger.dart). Server: no request id anywhere, and NO per-request log line at all, because uvicorn runs with `access_log=False` (server/encore_server/encore_server/__main__.py:43) on purpose: the music-server login travels in the query string (`u`, `t`, `s`, B-5) and a signed address carries `?sig=`, so a normal access log would write logins into the log.

THE TRAP: do not turn the access log back on to get ids. Write ONE line per request yourself, in a small ASGI middleware next to `InFlightMiddleware` and `BodyLimit` (api.py:1475-1476; the last one added is the outermost): request id, device id, method, the route TEMPLATE (`/likes/{ref_id}`, never the raw path or the query), status, milliseconds. Take `X-Request-Id` from the request when it is a well-formed ULID, otherwise make one; return it in the response header (the app logs it when a call fails); put it in a `contextvars` variable and add a logging filter so every other server log line made during the request carries it. Sync routes run in the thread pool: check that the context reaches them (Starlette copies it; prove it with a test, do not assume).

TWO NAMES FOR ONE HEADER: docs/24 section 1 says `X-Device-Id`; code and server say `X-Encore-Device` (api.py:145). The code is the fact: change the document. The header is the legacy door's way to name a device and goes away with P3-03 (a device token), so spend no effort on it beyond the log field.

SCOPE OF "EVERY REQUEST": Encore API calls (`_send`), plus the three that bypass it and cannot set headers freely: the player's stream (just_audio can pass headers for a source), downloads (background_downloader takes headers) and cover images (cached image headers). List which of the three get the id in the PR; a stream without it can use the request id the server made and logged.

TESTS: server/encore_server/tests/test_logging.py has one test (no login tokens in the music-server client's logs, line 10): add "a request line carries an id and never the query string" (send a request with `?t=secret&s=salt` and a sig, grep the captured records), "a supplied id is kept, a malformed one replaced", "a log line made inside a sync route has the id". App: a test that `_send` adds the header and that `scrubSecrets` leaves an id alone.

DOCS in the same PR: docs/24 section 1 (header name; the id also in the response), register B-32 (mark closed), and P1-06's board mark stays what it is.
